title: Migration merkle leaf omits reciever; destination bound only by signature
description: verifyDepositsAndInternalBalances computes the merkle leaf as keccak256(abi.encode(account, deposits, internalBalances, ownerRoots)) (line 127). The destination `reciever` is NOT part of the leaf and therefore not committed to by the immutable MERKLE_ROOT. The only thing binding the credit to a specific L2 destination is the owner's EIP-712 signature over (owner,reciever,deadline) in verifySignature. This splits authorization across two artifacts (a root that fixes WHAT migrates, and a signature that fixes WHERE it goes) without binding them together. Because the signature is plain calldata and AC-001 allows unlimited replay, the receiver binding provides no protection against reuse, and the absence of `reciever` from the proof means the proof can never constrain the destination. If a publisher ever signs more than one (owner,reciever) pair for the same owner-leaf, or the signature is otherwise obtainable, credit destination is governed solely by an unprotected, replayable signature rather than by the committed root. This weakens the authorization model and compounds AC-001.
impact: Authorization of the migration destination is decoupled from the merkle commitment and rests entirely on a single unprotected signature. Combined with AC-001 (no nonce/spent-marker) the destination binding is ineffective against replay. Standalone: incorrect/weak access binding of migrated credit. Immunefi v2.2: incorrect access binding without standalone direct loss = Medium.

ite.intent: Determine the destination of migrated credit independent of the on-chain merkle commitment
ite.technique: reciever is excluded from the merkle leaf; only the replayable EIP-712 signature binds it, so the committed root never constrains where credit lands
ite.evasion: Intended protection (a fixed merkle root committing the migration) does not cover the destination field; binding is delegated to a signature that AC-001 shows is reusable

ice_chain.impact: Migrated credit can be directed by signature alone rather than the committed root; amplifies replay reach of AC-001
ice_chain.consumer_function: addMigratedDepositsToAccount / setStalk write to s.accts[reciever] which feeds Silo and governance
ice_chain.exploit_path: Proof accepts any reciever -> reciever bound only by replayable signature (AC-001) -> credit lands at attacker-influenced/repeated destination
